steps.title: Select gage and data type
steps.instruction: Open the USGS Water Data portal (https://waterdata.usgs.gov/), choose the state of interest (e.g., Texas), select "Gage height" from the list of data types, navigate to the desired catchment, click a specific gage (e.g., 08165500) and open its "View Monitoring location page".

steps.title: Set analysis time span
steps.instruction: Click "Change time span" and enter the start and end dates for the period to be analyzed (e.g., October 12‑18, 2018) to capture the flash‑flood event, then apply the change.

steps.title: Download continuous data
steps.instruction: After the graph updates, click "Download data", choose the "Continuous data" option, and press "Retrieve" to open a .txt file containing the selected data.

steps.title: Import data into Excel
steps.instruction: In the new window, copy all columns beginning with the column labeled "agency_cd". Open Microsoft Excel, right‑click a cell, choose Paste Special → Text to paste the data into separate columns.

steps.title: Remove duplicate timestamps
steps.instruction: Select the entire sheet, go to Data → Remove Duplicates, keep only the date/time column (Column C) checked and deselect all other columns, then confirm removal to avoid division‑by‑zero errors later.

steps.title: Delete non‑15‑minute records
steps.instruction: In Column C, use Find & Replace to locate any time stamps ending with :05, :10, :20, :25, :35, :40, :50, or :55 and replace them with the string "!!!!". Sort the sheet by Column C (newest to oldest); rows containing "!!!!" will appear at the top—delete those rows. Finally, re‑sort by Column C oldest‑to‑newest to restore chronological order.

steps.title: Convert timestamps to hours
steps.instruction: Copy Column C to a new column and format the new column as Number (this converts the date/time to decimal days, placed in Column G). Create a "Corrected Time" column (Column H) and enter H2 = G2*24; copy the formula down to convert days to hours.

steps.title: Compute first derivative
steps.instruction: Label Column I "1st derivative". In I2 enter the formula =(E2‑E1)/(H2‑H1) (gage height in ft divided by time difference in hours) and copy the formula down the column.

steps.title: Compute second derivative
steps.instruction: Label Column J "2nd derivative". In J2 enter the formula =(I3‑I2)/(H3‑H2) to obtain the rate of change of the first derivative (acceleration) and copy the formula down.

steps.title: Calculate height‑times‑acceleration
steps.instruction: Label Column K "Height times acceleration". In K2 enter =E2*J2 to multiply gage height (ft) by its acceleration (ft/hr²) and copy the formula down the column.

steps.title: Determine maximum threshold
steps.instruction: Identify the maximum value in Column K (e.g., 313.8 ft²/hr² for the example storm). Record this value as the water‑height‑×‑acceleration threshold (WHAT) for the gage.

steps.title: Repeat for additional gages
steps.instruction: Apply the entire workflow to each other gage in the catchment to obtain their respective WHAT values.
